title: Yarn over (yo)
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), fig. 353. Public domain. Mary Thomas, Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938). Out of copyright UK/EU. The between-purl-and-knit and between-knit-and-purl positions are described in Weldon's Practical Knitter series (1880s). Public domain.

glossaryTerms.definition: A wrap of the working yarn over the right needle between stitches, creating a new loop. Worked as a stitch on the following row, it leaves an eyelet hole below it.
Knitted fabric with a regular pattern of eyelet holes formed by yarn overs balanced with matching decreases.
A deliberate hole in knitted fabric, formed by a yarn over paired with a decrease on the same row.

content.text: The secret of the
yarn over

(abbreviated yo) is simply the yarn wrapped once around the needle without entering any stitch. This creates a new stitch. On the return row it leaves an eyelet hole. All lace knitting is built from this one action paired with a decrease.
You need yarn and needles. Practise on a flat swatch of at least 15 stitches in a smooth yarn so the eyelet holes read clearly.

content.text: Step by step
The wrap position depends on the stitches on either side. The three most common situations are covered below.
Between two knit stitches (the standard lace yarn over):
After working the knit stitch before the yo, the yarn is already at the back.
Bring the yarn forward between the needle tips, then take it back over the top of the right needle. The yarn has now made one complete wrap around the right needle.
Work the next knit stitch in the usual way. You now have an extra loop on the right needle.
On the following row, work the yo loop as a regular stitch (knit or purl as the pattern directs). This opens the eyelet hole below it.
Between a purl and a knit stitch:
After the purl stitch the yarn is already at the front. Take it over the top of the right needle and back to the back. This single movement is the yo.
Between a knit and a purl stitch (yarn forward):
After the knit stitch, bring the yarn forward between the needle tips, over the top of the right needle, and forward again between the tips. The yarn ends at the front ready for the next purl.
Where you'll see it
Yarn overs are the foundation of all
lace
knitting. Each yarn over is paired with a decrease to keep the stitch count the same. They also appear in
eyelet
buttonholes (one yo with a k2tog removes one stitch and adds one back), in increases where the hole is wanted, and in brioche knitting where the yo and slip stitch together form the brioche unit.
Common faults
Missed yarn over. The yarn is brought forward but not taken over the needle, so no new stitch is formed. Check that the yarn completes a full wrap over the needle tip before the next stitch.

Accidental double yo. Taking the yarn forward, over, forward again and over again before the next knit stitch wraps the needle twice. Unless the pattern calls for a double yo, this adds an unwanted stitch.
Eyelet closed on the return row. If the yo loop is worked
through the back loop
, it twists closed and the hole disappears. On the return row, insert the needle into the front leg of the yo as for a standard stitch.
What to try next: combine yarn overs with
k2tog
and
ssk
to begin working simple lace patterns.
